title.narrative: OVOF Use of Arts Media and Culture - Uganda

description.narrative: Our Voices Our Futures (OVOF) partners bring extensive experience of lobbying and advocacy at multiple levels to a range of issues connected to gender, sexuality and digital rights. OVOF partners ensure that ground-level evidence and lived realities of structurally silenced women feed directly into lobbying and advocacyat every level and international-level advocacy is translated back into community-level work in the six countries. More international and national-level law and policymakers need to acknowledge and address the issue of growing authoritarianism (and its impact on civic space, democracy and the lives of structurally silenced women) and the increasing influence of anti-gender and anti-rights actors within international and national policy and legal spaces. Key Dutch actors will be mobilised to collaborate with and support Women Human Rights Defenders, LBT activists and sex workers’ rights movements by creating and opening spaces for their participation in international processes such as the Commission on the Status of Women and the Human Rights Council so that their voices will be heard.

At least 1 initiative or activity relating to arts, culture and media initiatives in Uganda aims to be undertaken by structurally silenced women.

An organisation led by Structurally Silenced Women was supported to produce an animated video creating awareness about the lived realities of Structurally Silenced Women and their rights. The animated video is in post-production phase i.e. designing and reviewing the content captured. This animated video result will be reported in FY2023 results once its production has been completed. One other organisation was supported to produce podcasts that has enabled the partner to reach more LBQ women with relevant information, which has inspired many of them to reach out for psychosocial support, community building and access to healthcare services. Results under this activity will be reported for in FY2023 results.
At least 1 initiative or activity relating to arts, culture and media initiatives in Uganda aims to be undertaken by structurally silenced women.

In addition to results under Output 2.3.1, several partners continued to harnessed arts, culture, and media platforms to amplify the lived experiences, resistance, and narratives of structurally silenced women, with significant reach and resonance across Uganda. Collectively, these creative interventions challenged dominant harmful discourses, centered the voices of structurally silenced women, and expanded public consciousness around digital and gender justice. The combination of grassroots digital campaigns, national broadcast media, and public art spaces marked a significant contribution toward shifting Uganda’s cultural and political narratives to be more inclusive, intersectional, and rights-affirming.

UGANDA 1-Creation of social media networks to strengthen community solidarity during implementation of AHA2023 which resulted in further isolation of SSW/Cs, some of whom were disowned by their families due to polarising public discourse on LGBT rights. 2-Addressed mis/disinformation on digital platforms that perpetuated violence against LGBTQ+ persons in Uganda. SSW/C community members were provided with information that sought to affirm their humanity and to also inform them of available resources and LGBTQ+ community structures that could offer psychosocial support and other forms of solidarity. 3-Data protection: Partner was supported to back it organisational and client digital data on safer digital platforms. This is a security protocol that also increased the safety of the Staff and community members in the event the office premises were raided or if their digital systems were hacked.

UHAI partner procured essential materials—including paint, canvas, brushes, oils, paper, and frames for the studio—and ensured the space remained accessible to the community. The partner continued to operate and maintain a dedicated art studio as a safe and creative space for structurally excluded womxn. Beyond art-making, the studio served as a healing and reflective space where womxn could connect, express their struggles, and process trauma through creativity. In a time of national uncertainty and repression, the studio emerged as a crucial site of therapy, solidarity, and resistance for art activists navigating stress.UHAI partner social media advocacy - the partner significantly expanded its digital footprint through active advocacy on platforms such as X (formerly Twitter) and Facebook. These platforms were strategically used to amplify the voices of minority and marginalized communities, raise awareness on key issues, and mobilize public support.
